abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) captures gene expression with spatial context but often at resolutions where each spatial location contains multiple cells. Deconvolution of cell-type proportions is therefore essential, yet existing methods typically rely on a single scRNA-seq reference, limiting accuracy when references are incomplete or mismatched especially in complex tissues. These limitations highlight the need for a framework that can integrate multiple references while leveraging spatial information. We introduce SWIMR (Spatially Weighted Integration for Multi-Reference deconvolution), a statistical framework that integrates multiple scRNA-seq references while accounting for spatial correlations. SWIMR models each spatial location as a weighted combination of references, with both cell-type proportions and reference weights varying across tissue locations. Across comprehensive simulations and diverse ST datasets, SWIMR consistently outperformed single-reference approaches. In developing human heart tissue, it recovered ground-truth cell-type compositions with the highest accuracy. In human lung and breast cancer, SWIMR delineated tumor, stromal, and immune compartments, uncovered tumor-adjacent populations, and detected cell type-specific spatially variable genes missed by other methods. In mouse embryo and liver cancer, it leveraged context-specific references to resolve organ-specific cell types and increase sensitivity for biologically relevant pathways. Together, these results establish SWIMR as a robust framework for multi-reference deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics.
